known_facts_book1: A very tall soldier in green and gold with a jewelled belt and a long green beard falling far below his waist.
Is at once the Body-Guard of Ozma, the whole Royal Army of Oz and the Police Force of the Emerald City, and is addressed indifferently as Colonel and General.
Had nothing to do in his official positions for so many years that he began to fear he was useless, until Ojo's arrest.
Arrests Ojo at the city gate on Ozma's orders and snaps golden handcuffs set with rubies and diamonds over his wrists.
Delivers Ojo to Tollydiggle the jailer and takes a receipt for him.
Reports that Billina has hatched out thirteen new chickens, about seven thousand chicks in all.

known_relations_book1.Ojo: The first prisoner he has ever arrested, whom he treats courteously throughout.
known_relations_book1.Ozma: The Ruler whose orders he obeys and whose body-guard he is.
known_relations_book1.Tollydiggle: The jailer to whom he hands the prisoner over.
known_relations_book1.Shaggy Man: Greets him familiarly at the gate as an old acquaintance.

known_facts_book1: The jailer of the only prison in the Land of Oz, a pretty house beside the city wall with a flower garden in front.
Had never had anything to do in her official capacity until Ojo was brought to her.
Keeps a prison whose windows have no locks and whose three doors are never bolted, with a domed roof of colored glass, gold-panelled walls, books and a cupboard of games.
Cooks Ojo mutton-chops with gravy for supper, sits sewing beside him while he eats, and reads him a story.
Explains Ozma's theory of punishment: a prisoner is unfortunate twice over, so kindness is what makes him strong and brave enough not to do wrong again.

known_relations_book1.Ojo: Her first and only prisoner, whom she treats as a guest.
known_relations_book1.Soldier with the Green Whiskers: Delivers the prisoner to her and takes her receipt.
known_relations_book1.Ozma: The Ruler whose philosophy of kindness to prisoners she explains.

known_facts_book1: A jolly little man richly dressed in green, wearing a heavy gold chain hung with great golden keys, who keeps the room inside the city gate.
Composes a mouth-organ tune called 'The Speckled Alligator', in patch-time, in honour of the Patchwork Girl's arrival.
Says it is his business to know who is coming, since he is the Guardian of the Gate.
Fetches the white prisoner's robe from the Official Wardrobe for Ojo — a robe covering him head to foot with two holes for the eyes.
Is astonished at the very idea of a prisoner, saying no one ever breaks the Law.

known_facts_book1: The favorite servant-maid of the royal palace.
Announces the Shaggy Man to Dorothy and reports that he has some of the queerest creatures she has ever laid eyes on with him.
Is proposed by Dorothy as the one to keep the Glass Cat until Ojo returns.
Wheels forward the chair Ozma sits in for the final scene in which the statues are restored.
Takes no part in the plot beyond these palace duties.
